column7: Fannie Mae Q2-2026 earnings release PDF (PRIMARY, pdfminer-extracted 2026-07-31)
column9: ★ MEASUREMENT, NOT CREDIT — issuer says so in its own words. Quarter-end series 2Q25 0.61 / 3Q25 0.68 / 4Q25 0.74 / 1Q26 0.78 / 2Q26 0.60. Fannie's stated driver, verbatim: decline "primarily as a result of the modification of a loan portfolio previously in forbearance and foreclosure activity, partially offset by additional loans that became seriously delinquent due to sustained market challenges in recent periods." BOTH removal channels (mod + foreclosure) take loans OUT of the numerator without any borrower cure; the inflow of newly-serious loans CONTINUED. DEFINITION (footnote 11): MF loans 60+ days past due, by UNPAID PRINCIPAL BALANCE (not loan count) — so a single large modified portfolio moves the rate hard. Do NOT read as GSE-MF credit improvement.

Stated driver: "stress from elevated interest rates and small balance loans." ⚠️ TWO CAVEATS, both open: (1) SOURCE — Freddie's own site and the EDGAR 8-K both returned 403 this session; figure rests on StockTitan's 10-Q summary + a second search agreeing. Needs PRIMARY confirmation next session. (2) ★ "NEW HIGH?" PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-31 — AND THE ANSWER IS "WHICH SERIES?" There are TWO non-interchangeable Freddie MF series and they disagree. (i) QUARTERLY (10-Q "multifamily delinquency rate"): Q2-25 0.47 / Q4-25 0.44 / Q2-26 0.51 — this matches HOMER's carried ledger exactly (Q1 0.46, Q2 0.47, Q3 0.51, Q4 0.44), and on it Q2-26 TIES the Q3-25 0.51 rather than exceeding it. (ii) MONTHLY (Monthly Volume Summary "serious delinquency rate"): Oct-25 0.48 / Nov-25 0.48, with the PRIOR PEAK documented at 0.39% — already exceeded during 2025, so on THIS series 0.51% is a genuine multi-decade high and the "highest since financial crisis" headline is defensible. CONCLUSION: the headline is probably right ON THE MONTHLY SERIES and wrong-or-unproven on the quarterly one; HOMER's 0.51% Q2 figure is QUARTERLY, so DO NOT attach the monthly series' record framing to it. ★ Q3-25 = 0.51% NOW INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED (2026-07-31): MBA Commercial/Multifamily Delinquency Report for Q3-2025 (rel 2025-12-04) has Freddie MF ending Q3-25 at 0.51%, +0.04pp from Q2-25's 0.47% — matching HOMER's carried ledger exactly on BOTH points. SO THE TIE READING IS VERIFIED, NOT MERELY SUSPECTED: Q2-2026's 0.51% TIES Q3-2025 on the quarterly series and is NOT a new high there. Publishing "post-GFC high" against the quarterly figure would have been WRONG — the 7/31 caution was correct. Residual gap: Q1-2026 quarterly value not yet held (the Q2 source compared to Q4-25, skipping it); and the MBA report is a different compiler than Freddie's own 10-Q, so treat as corroboration rather than identity. ★ THE SESSION'S CORE FINDING — the "GSE book" is not one book and stopped moving as one. Same quarter, same asset class, opposite directions. The agency with a large one-off modification event (Fannie) improved; the agency without one (Freddie) deteriorated to its band edge. That asymmetry is itself evidence that Fannie's move is a RECOGNITION-REGIME artifact rather than multifamily credit healing — and it is exactly the shape the CRL-03 resolution's surviving mechanism note predicted. NOTE both GSE metrics are 60+ days; Trepp CMBS DQ is 30+ days over a different universe — the three are NOT like-for-like levels, only like-for-like DIRECTIONS.

column9: ★★ THE MOST USEFUL MF NUMBER OF THE 7/31 SWEEP — a HARD, OBSERVED multifamily mark, not a modeled one. BANC moved $827.0M of loans to held-for-sale at lower-of-cost-or-market; the block is 94% MULTIFAMILY ($491.9M multifamily + $300.6M multifamily construction + $34.5M CRE mortgage). Provision jumped to $161.8M from $9.8M in Q1 on $161.6M of charge-offs; annualized NCOs 2.54% of avg loans vs 0.23% prior quarter; loss to common $(251.3)M / $(1.61)/sh. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE BANK: every loss-severity assumption in the MF complex is currently MODELED; this is a lender choosing to SELL rather than extend and printing the realized haircut publicly. Anchor loss-severity work to this rather than to a model until contradicted. ⚠️ CAVEATS: the ~19.5% is an IMPLIED average across a mixed block (construction loans plausibly carry a worse mark than stabilized MF, so the stabilized-MF severity is likely BETTER than 19.5% and the construction severity WORSE) — do not apply it as a uniform per-loan severity; and a lower-of-cost-or-market transfer is a SALE decision, so it embeds a liquidity/exit discount, not a pure credit view. Route to REGINALD (Path C — bank realizing MF marks).
